partners.mechanism_chain: APC variant leading to haploinsufficiency (None) —DISRUPTS→ APC (HGNC:424); APC (HGNC:424) —DECREASES→ Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP528); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP528) —INCREASES→ CTNNB1 (HGNC:2515); CTNNB1 (HGNC:2515) —LEADS_TO→ Orofacial cleft (HP:0000218); APC loss-of-function variant (None) —DISRUPTS→ APC (HGNC:424); APC (HGNC:424) —DECREASES→ Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP528); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP528) —INCREASES→ CTNNB1 (HGNC:2515); CTNNB1 (HGNC:2515) —LEADS_TO→ Colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575). This hypothesis proposes that dysregulation of the Wnt signaling pathway, driven by variants in the APC gene, is a shared mechanism. In orofacial cleft 11, haploinsufficiency of APC leads to insufficient negative regulation of Wnt signaling, impacting craniofacial development. In colorectal cancer, loss-of-function mutations in APC result in constitutive Wnt signaling, promoting uncontrolled cell proliferation and tumorigenesis. Both disease mechanisms converge on the Wnt signaling pathway and the downstream effects mediated by CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) stabilization.
